text:
Kris Letang has played 1,257 games, all in Pittsburgh, won three Cups and a Masterton, and at 39 he's now a name in fire-sale headlines. The New York Times asked where Crosby, Malkin and Letang go from here with the Penguins' season spiraling, and one report says Pittsburgh "can't find trade market" for him.

On the ice, he's still doing his job. Ten points in 22 games (one goal, nine assists) is right on his range, and Pittsburgh takes 55.5% of the expected goals at five on five with him out there, 4.7 points better than without him. His team has actually scored 5.8 more goals than its chances with him on the ice. His own shooting has gone the other way: one goal on 2.1 expected, at 2.5%.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says he's a setup man, 6.4 primary shot assists per 60 (93rd percentile among defensemen); the next shot is often a teammate's. His wins-added number ranks near the bottom of the league, but that measure counts goals, and he has one. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season. The question for Pittsburgh isn't whether he can still pass; it's whether anyone wants him.
